thread:
Kira: In today's design review we discussed adding a 'soft cap' annotation to the autoscale min/max controls. idea: show soft cap (recommended upper bound) vs hard cap (absolute max) so teams understand guardrails. mock: https://redwood.app/s/ux/23145
Ravi: love the annotation. question: how does soft cap behave when users drag the max slider past it? subtle inline warning or a more prominent guardrail?
Jun: proposal: inline amber hint under the slider that reads: 'Soft cap: recommended max for cost/stability'. If user exceeds, show a non-blocking inline message: 'Above recommended capacity  review cost impacts.' with a link to docs.
Noor: accessibility: make sure soft cap indicator is programmatically exposed (aria-describedby) and that reaching/exceeding it triggers an aria-live polite message: "Warning: above recommended capacity." Also ensure color isn't the only cue.
Ava: microcopy tweak: avoid ambiguous words like "recommended". Suggest: 'Soft cap (recommended for typical workloads)'. Keep hard cap label 'Max (hard limit)'.
Kira: second UX item: stepper acceleration on long press for min/max steppers on mobile and desktop. currently holding arrow increments too slowly for large changes.
Ravi: we can implement exponential step acceleration: hold -> 1/sec then 4/sec after 500ms then 10/sec. but need to indicate this behavior so it's discoverable.
Jun: inline affordance: tooltip on hover/mouse down that says "Hold to speed up"; on mobile show a brief toast when you long-press the +/- showing current pace.
Noor: accessibility concerns: long-press acceleration must be keyboard-accessible. For keyboard users, implement repeated keydown acceleration (holding ArrowUp/Down) and expose an accessible control attribute like `aria-live` announcing pace change: "Accelerating: 4 items per second". Also provide a way to jump by 5 or 10 via modifier (Shift+Arrow to add 5, Alt+Arrow to add 10) with visible hint.
Ava: good point. add microcopy under the stepper: "Hold to accelerate. Shift+Arrow +5, Alt+Arrow +10." Keep this concise and ensure contrast.
Kira: UI layout question: where should soft cap marker sit? overlay on the slider track (thin dashed line) or as a small pin above the track with label? Which reads better on mobile?
Ravi: overlay pin with tooltip might be occluded on small screens. dashed line with subtle label to the right of track seems cleaner and less likely to overlap other controls.
Jun: implement dashed line using pseudo-element `::after` positioned at percentage based on value. label can be visually hidden on very small widths and exposed via aria-describedby for SRs.
Noor: ensure that the soft cap marker isn't the only indicator  add `role/status` text update when the handle crosses it. e.g., "Handle crossed recommended cap" announced once.
Kira: prototyping plan: Jun will push `feature/soft-cap-stepper-23145` with two mocks: desktop and mobile. design-bot will attach them.
design-bot: uploaded files: softcap_desktop.png, softcap_mobile.png; created branch feature/soft-cap-stepper-23145
Ava: microtest plan: 1) Keyboard: Tab to stepper, hold ArrowUp for 3s, ensure acceleration and SR announcements. 2) Mouse: hold + button and verify tooltip and acceleration. 3) Mobile: long-press increments and soft cap dashed line visible. 3 engineers, 15m.
Noor: i'll run accessibility checks (NVDA/VoiceOver/JAWS) after branch lands. I'll verify aria-live messages, modifier key hints, and that color is not sole indicator.
Ravi: i'll look at performance implications of pseudo-element marker for big batches and ensure no layout thrash.
Kira: thanks everyone. i'll update the product doc with final copy suggestions and link to the PR when ready
